title: The Songbook of Sandpiper Point
premise: Quentin Voss, a pastry chef drowning in debt at his failing Sandpiper Point café, discovers his late grandmother's orchard deed lists two names: his own and that of Marisol Reyes, the woman he loved and abandoned twelve years ago to save his family's business. Forced into reluctant partnership to save the orchard from a developer's deadline, they rebuild trust one harvest at a time while Quentin confronts the memory of what his survival cost. When the developer makes a final offer that would erase both their debts, Quentin must choose between financial salvation and the love he once traded away. He refuses the offer, they save the orchard together through a community co-op, and on the last chapter's autumn night he finally speaks of love in the present tense.
about_author: Felix Winterbourne is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, coastlines, and the quiet spaces where duty collides with desire. He lives in a coastal town much like Sandpiper Point, where he bakes bread badly and collects old deeds.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Opening in his struggling café, we see him counting coins, dodging the bank, and baking with mechanical precision—grief disguised as routine. A letter arrives about his grandmother's estate. Emotional beat: numb survival cracked open by an unexpected summons.

chapters.title: The Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the county records office he learns the orchard deed names both him and Marisol Reyes—the woman he left without goodbye a dozen years ago. The lawyer warns of a developer's standing offer and a 90-day deadline. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into inevitability.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She arrives at the overgrown orchard expecting paperwork, not Quentin. Their first meeting is all barbed civility and unfinished sentences. She reveals she nearly bought the orchard herself last year. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened under new light.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They negotiate an uneasy truce: she handles the land, he caters an orchard fundraiser to pay back taxes. Working side by side, small kindnesses slip through the armor—a remembered coffee order, a laugh neither planned. Emotional beat: cautious thaw.

chapters.title: The Year He Didn't Write
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A rainstorm traps them in the farmhouse; she finally demands the truth of why he vanished. Quentin confesses his father's debts and the choice that felt like betrayal but felt like survival. Emotional beat: confession without absolution—yet.

chapters.title: Blossoms Out of Season
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Spring work becomes intimacy: grafting trees, sharing meals, a kiss in the cold barn that both immediately regret and don't. But Marisol finds the developer's earlier letter in Quentin's coat—proof he'd considered selling alone. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: The Offer on the Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The developer returns with a doubled offer that would clear Quentin's café debt entirely. Marisol, stung, pulls away; Quentin, ashamed, almost signs. His grandmother's letters surface, revealing she paired their names deliberately. Emotional beat: the past tense collapsing.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, One Night
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Deadline eve. He closes the café for good—or so it seems—and drives through the storm to the orchard, where Marisol is burning her own escape plans in the woodstove. They choose each other aloud, fully, no pieces lent. Emotional beat: whole-hearted surrender.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Climax. At the courthouse auction, the developer bids against them with money they can't match—until Quentin's regulars, Marisol's farming neighbors, and the town arrive with pooled savings and a co-op charter. The gavel falls on community, not capital. Emotional beat: triumph earned collectively.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Autumn harvest: the café reopens as an orchard kitchen, the first cider pressed, Quentin's grandmother's tree bearing fruit. On the porch he says 'I love you' in the present tense for the first time. Emotional beat: peace—the price of survival finally paid in full, and refunded by love.
